Baldwin County: 1,177 people in reported Housing Choice Voucher households in 2025
HUD’s 2025 figures show 415 reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Baldwin County, Alabama.
Reported Housing Choice Voucher households in Baldwin County included 1,177 people in 2025, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.
The number of people was down 13 from 1,190 in 2024. Those people lived in 415 households.
73% of those households were headed by a person HUD classifies as a racial or ethnic minority. Households paid an average of $493 a month toward rent and utilities, up $35 from $458 in 2024, and their average annual household income was $19,024, up $1,087 from $17,937 in 2024.
The federal Housing Choice Voucher program helps eligible households rent privately owned homes. Participants generally contribute about 30% of their adjusted monthly income toward rent and utilities, while a local housing agency pays a subsidy to the landlord, according to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. A household may pay more if it chooses a home whose rent exceeds the agency's payment standard.
In 2024, families who received Housing Choice Vouchers had spent an average of 29 months on waiting lists, according to the . This average applies to families who obtained assistance, not applicants who were still waiting or never served. HUD also estimates that only one in four eligible families receives federal rental assistance.
